\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{کسکنا} (kasaknā)}{کسکنا (kasaknā)}]{\ur{کسکنا} (kasaknā) — to ache dully; to twinge}

\label{lesson:UR-C473-kasakna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for retching, then the Urdu for nourishment.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{کسکنا}}
\textbf{\ur{کسکنا}} — \emph{kasaknā} — \textquotedblleft{}to ache dully; to twinge\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{سردی} \ur{میں} \ur{پرانا} \ur{زخم} \ur{کسکتا} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sardī meṅ purānā zakhm kasaktā hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The old wound aches in the cold.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \ur{وہ} \ur{زخم} \ur{رات} \ur{بھر} \ur{کسکا}, \emph{voh zakhm rāt bhar kaskā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{کسکنا}} (\emph{kasaknā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{kasaknā}, \textquotedblleft{}to ache\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{kaṣati}, \textquotedblleft{}scratches\textquotedblright{}, which an old list of roots also gives as \textquotedblleft{}hurts\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 2972).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kasaknā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kasaknā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sardī meṅ purānā zakhm kasaktā hai.} — The old wound aches in the cold.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for retching, then the Urdu for nourishment, then say \emph{kasaknā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{کسکنا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To ache dully; to twinge\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{اینٹھن} (aiṅṭhan)}{اینٹھن (aiṅṭhan)}]{\ur{اینٹھن} (aiṅṭhan) — a cramp}

\label{lesson:UR-C473-ainthan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for nourishment, then the Urdu for to ache dully.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{اینٹھن}}
\textbf{\ur{اینٹھن}} — \emph{aiṅṭhan} — \textquotedblleft{}a cramp\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{تیرنے} \ur{کے} \ur{بعد} \ur{پنڈلی} \ur{میں} \ur{اینٹھن} \ur{ہوئی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tairne ke bād pinḍlī meṅ aiṅṭhan huī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I got a cramp in my calf after swimming.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{اینٹھن}} (\emph{aiṅṭhan}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{aĩṭhan}, \textquotedblleft{}a twist\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{āvēṣṭana}, \textquotedblleft{}wrapping round\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 1449): a cramp twists the muscle.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aiṅṭhan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aiṅṭhan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tairne ke bād pinḍlī meṅ aiṅṭhan huī.} — I got a cramp in my calf after swimming.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for nourishment, then the Urdu for to ache dully, then say \emph{aiṅṭhan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{جکڑنا} (jakaṛnā)}{جکڑنا (jakaṛnā)}]{\ur{جکڑنا} (jakaṛnā) — to grip tight; to stiffen}

\label{lesson:UR-C473-jakarna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to ache dully, then the Urdu for a cramp.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{جکڑنا}}
\textbf{\ur{جکڑنا}} — \emph{jakaṛnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to grip tight; to stiffen\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{سردی} \ur{میں} \ur{میری} \ur{کمر} \ur{جکڑ} \ur{گئی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sardī meṅ merī kamar jakaṛ gaī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My back stiffened up in the cold.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{رسی} \ur{جکڑی}, \emph{us ne rassī jakṛī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{جکڑنا}} (\emph{jakaṛnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{jakaṛnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to tighten, to bind\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{yatá}, \textquotedblleft{}restrained\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 10400).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{لنگڑانا} (laṅgṛānā)}{لنگڑانا (laṅgṛānā)}]{\ur{لنگڑانا} (laṅgṛānā) — to limp}

\label{lesson:UR-C473-langrana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a cramp, then the Urdu for to grip tight.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{لنگڑانا}}
\textbf{\ur{لنگڑانا}} — \emph{laṅgṛānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to limp\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{چوٹ} \ur{کے} \ur{بعد} \ur{وہ} \ur{لنگڑا} \ur{رہا} \ur{تھا۔}
\end{quote}

Past (he …): \ur{وہ} \ur{لنگڑایا}, \emph{voh laṅgṛāyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{لنگڑانا}} (\emph{laṅgṛānā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{lãgṛānā}, \textquotedblleft{}to limp\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{lakka}, \textquotedblleft{}defective\textquotedblright{}, with Sanskrit \emph{laṅga}, \textquotedblleft{}lame\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 10877).

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{سوزش} (sozish)}{سوزش (sozish)}]{\ur{سوزش} (sozish) — an inflammation}

\label{lesson:UR-C473-sozish}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to grip tight, then the Urdu for to limp.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{سوزش}}
\textbf{\ur{سوزش}} — \emph{sozish} — \textquotedblleft{}an inflammation\textquotedblright{}.
